Source format: committee charter

2.2 In fulfilling its purpose, the Council shall have regard to the differing circumstances of consumers, including those who may be particularly vulnerable to product-related injury, and to the interests of industry in achieving compliance without undue regulatory burden.

**Functions**

3.1 The principal functions of the Council are:

(a) to receive and consider reports from Commonwealth, State, and Territory regulators on product safety investigations, recalls, and compliance activities;

(b) to identify and advise on priorities for product safety action, including the development or revision of mandatory safety standards, bans, and information standards;

(c) to provide a forum for the early identification of emerging hazards arising from new or modified consumer products, including those associated with technological change;

(d) to advise on the design and conduct of public information campaigns relating to product safety;

(e) to review, from time to time, the operation of product safety provisions of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 and related legislation, and to recommend amendments or administrative improvements;

(f) to establish working groups or subcommittees to examine particular product safety issues, and to receive and consider their reports;

(g) to liaise with corresponding bodies in other countries, and with international standard-setting organisations, on matters of mutual interest; and

(h) to perform such other functions as the Minister may from time to time direct in writing.

3.2 The Council may, at its discretion, make recommendations to the Minister on any matter within its functions. Recommendations shall be in writing and shall, where practicable, include an assessment of the expected benefits, costs, and impacts of the proposed action, including impacts on small business.

3.3 The Council shall not, without the prior agreement of the Minister, publish or otherwise disclose a recommendation or report that has not yet been considered by the Minister. This clause does not prevent the Council from publishing its annual report or other documents approved for publication by the Minister.

Australian Consumer Product Safety Advisory Council established 2015-03-01 date. Record status: current.

**Membership and Composition**

4.1 The Council shall consist of not fewer than nine (9) and not more than fifteen (15) members appointed by the Minister.

4.2 The membership shall include:

(a) a Chair, appointed by the Minister;

(b) one representative from each of the following Commonwealth agencies, nominated by the head of that agency and appointed by the Minister:

(i) the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission;

(ii) the Department of Health, being the agency responsible for the administration of the Consumer Product Safety Act;

(iii) the Department of Industry, Innovation and Science; and

(iv) the Australian Border Force;

(c) one representative from each of the State and Territory consumer affairs agencies, nominated by the relevant Minister of that State or Territory and appointed by the Commonwealth Minister;

(d) up to two (2) persons with expertise in consumer product safety, injury prevention, or related fields, appointed in a personal capacity; and

(e) up to two (2) persons representing the interests of industry, appointed in a personal capacity after consultation with relevant industry associations.

4.3 Appointments shall be for a term of up to three (3) years and may be renewed. A member may resign at any time by written notice to the Chair. The Minister may terminate an appointment at any time for inability to perform the functions of the office, misbehaviour, or other good cause.
**Membership and Composition (continued)**

4.4 In making an appointment under clause 4.2, the Minister shall have regard to:

(a) the need for the Council to include members with a range of skills, knowledge, and experience relevant to the Council’s functions;

(b) the desirability of the membership including persons from different geographic regions of Australia, including regional and remote areas;

(c) the need for the Council to include members who can represent the views of consumers, industry, and government respectively; and

(d) any other matter the Minister considers relevant.

4.5 A member appointed in a personal capacity under clause 4.2(d) or 4.2(e) shall be appointed by written instrument. The instrument shall specify the term of appointment and any conditions of appointment determined by the Minister.

4.6 A member appointed as a representative of a Commonwealth agency or of a State or Territory agency under clause 4.2(b) or 4.2(c) shall hold office as a representative of that agency. If the member ceases to be employed by, or otherwise associated with, that agency, the member shall be taken to have vacated office at the end of the day on which the member ceases that employment or association.

4.7 The Minister may appoint a person to act as Chair during any period when the Chair is absent from duty or unable to perform the functions of the office. A person appointed to act as Chair shall have the same functions and powers as the Chair while acting.

**Termination of Appointment and Casual Vacancies**

5.1 The office of a member becomes vacant if:

(a) the member resigns by written notice to the Chair;

(b) the Minister terminates the appointment under clause 4.3;

(c) the member ceases to be eligible for appointment; or

(d) the member dies.

5.2 Where a vacancy occurs, the Minister may appoint a person to fill the vacancy in accordance with the relevant provision of clause 4.2. A person appointed to fill a casual vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the vacated office.

5.3 The validity of any proceedings of the Council is not affected by a vacancy in the membership, or by a defect in the appointment of a member, provided that the Council continues to meet the quorum requirements in clause 6.2.

**Meetings and Quorum**

6.1 The Council shall meet at least four (4) times per financial year. Meetings shall be convened by the Chair, and the Chair shall convene a meeting within fourteen (14) days of receiving a written request from the Minister or from at least one-third of the members.

6.2 At a meeting of the Council, a quorum shall be constituted by one-half of the members holding office at the time of the meeting, rounded up to the nearest whole number, provided that at least one of those members is the Chair or the acting Chair.

6.3 Questions arising at a meeting of the Council shall be determined by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The Chair, or the acting Chair, shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, a second or casting vote.

6.4 A member who has a material personal interest in a matter being considered by the Council shall disclose that interest to the Council, and the member shall not be present during any deliberation or decision of the Council on that matter. The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

6.5 The Council may invite persons to attend a meeting or part of a meeting to assist the Council in its deliberations. A person invited under this clause does not have a vote.
**Meetings and Quorum (continued)**

6.6 The Chair shall preside at every meeting of the Council at which the Chair is present. If the Chair is not present within fifteen (15) minutes after the time appointed for the meeting, or if the Chair is unable to act, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting. A member elected to preside under this clause shall, for the purposes of that meeting, have the same powers and duties as the Chair, including the power to exercise a casting vote.

6.7 Subject to clause 6.2, the Council may transact business at a meeting only if a quorum is present at the time the meeting is convened and at the time any question is put to a vote. If a quorum is not present within thirty (30) minutes after the time appointed for a meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same time and place on the next available sitting day, or to such other time and place as the Chair determines. If a quorum is not present at the adjourned meeting within thirty (30) minutes after the time appointed, the members present may proceed with the business of the meeting, provided that they constitute at least three (3) members.

6.8 The Council shall cause minutes of each meeting to be kept. The minutes shall record:
(a) the names of the members present and of any persons invited under clause 6.5;
(b) all disclosures of material personal interests made under clause 6.4 and the manner in which the Council dealt with the matter;
(c) each question put to a vote, the number of votes cast for and against, and the names of any members who requested that their dissent be recorded; and
(d) any decision of the Council, including any direction given to the Executive Officer under clause 8.3.

6.9 Minutes of a meeting shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Council, or at such later meeting as the Council may determine. The minutes, once confirmed, shall be signed by the presiding member and retained by the Executive Officer. Subject to any direction of the Minister to the contrary, the confirmed minutes of each meeting shall be published on the Department's website within twenty (20) business days of confirmation, with any material excluded under clause 6.10.

6.10 The Council may resolve that any part of the minutes or any document tabled at a meeting be treated as confidential, where the Council considers that disclosure would:
(a) prejudice the commercial interests of any person;
(b) reveal information obtained in confidence from a person engaged in the supply of consumer goods; or
(c) otherwise be contrary to the public interest.
A resolution under this clause shall record the reasons for the decision and the period for which confidentiality is to apply.

6.11 The Council may meet by means of any technology that allows all participants to hear and be heard, or otherwise to communicate contemporaneously. A meeting held by such means is taken to be held at the place where the Chair is located at the commencement of the meeting. For the purposes of this clause, a member participating by telephone, video link, or other electronic means is taken to be present at the meeting.

6.12 A member may, with the prior approval of the Chair, appoint a substitute to attend a meeting in the member's place. A substitute appointed under this clause:
(a) must be a person with relevant expertise in consumer product safety;
(b) shall, for the purposes of that meeting, have the same rights and obligations as the member, including the right to vote; and
(c) shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting as attending in the place of the member.
A member may not appoint a substitute for more than two (2) consecutive meetings without the approval of the Council.

**2. WELCOME AND OPENING REMARKS**

The Chair called the meeting to order at 9:05 AM. Dr. Vance welcomed members to her first meeting as Chair, noting her appointment by the Office of Product Safety effective 1 January 2017. She acknowledged the outgoing Chair, Dr. Robert Fielding, for his service over the preceding four years, and thanked members for their continued commitment.

Dr. Vance stated her priorities for the coming term: (1) strengthening post-market surveillance data sharing between jurisdictions, (2) improving timeliness of recall notifications, and (3) ensuring the Council’s advice reflects the diversity of Australian consumers. She invited members to raise any procedural concerns during the meeting.

There being no objections, the agenda was adopted as circulated.

---

Members were reminded of their obligation to declare any conflicts of interest relevant to agenda items.

- Mr. Robert Sinclair declared an interest in Item 6 (Infant Sleep Products) as his organisation represents three manufacturers of infant hammocks.
- Ms. Lucy Hartley declared an interest in Item 5 (Treadmill Safety) as her retail group is a major importer of treadmills.
- Dr. Margaret Chen declared that her testing laboratory had recently completed commissioned testing for a brand of portable fans, relevant to Item 8.

No other declarations were made.

**5. TREADMILL SAFETY – REVIEW OF RECALL EFFECTIVENESS**

Ms. Lucy Hartley provided an update on the voluntary recall of the FitLife Treadmill Model T-500, first announced in September 2016. The recall was issued following reports of the treadmill continuing to run after the safety key was removed, resulting in two reported injuries.

Ms. Hartley reported that of the estimated 4,200 units sold in Australia, approximately 2,850 units had been returned or rendered inoperable as of 20 January 2017. This represented a completion rate of 68%. She noted that the recall notice had been re-issued in December 2016 with clearer instructions for consumers.

Mr. Peter Kowalski queried whether the recall effectiveness data had been disaggregated by state. Ms. Hartley indicated that it had not, but offered to request this from the importer.

The Chair noted that the ACCC’s Product Safety Australia website had received 1,200 hits on the recall page in December. She suggested that the Council might consider recommending a mandatory reporting requirement for recall completion rates in future.

**Discussion:** Mr. Graham Whitfield expressed caution about imposing mandatory reporting, noting the administrative burden on small importers. Ms. Helen Tran disagreed, stating that consumers needed greater transparency. After discussion, the Council agreed that the matter would be referred to the Product Safety Data Working Group for further examination.

**Action:** Secretariat to write to the importer (FitLife Australia) requesting state-by-state recall completion data, with a copy to all members. Due: 28 February 2017.

---
The Chair reported on correspondence received since the last meeting, including:

- A response from the Office of Product Safety (OPS) dated 18 November 2019 requesting a formal recommendation on the proposed changes to the mandatory standard for treadmills.
- A letter from a consumer organisation in Western Australia regarding the visibility of safety warnings on portable electric heaters.
- An invitation for the Council to nominate a representative to the joint working group on button battery safety, to be convened by the ACCC in early 2020.

The Chair noted that the correspondence from OPS would be addressed under item 4 of the agenda.

---

**3. PORTABLE ELECTRIC HEATER SAFETY – DISCUSSION FOLLOWING TESTING**

Mr. Graham Whitfield tabled a summary of the results of the recent round of joint testing conducted by the Council and the ACCC on portable electric heaters. Mr. Whitfield noted that of the twelve models tested, three failed the relevant safety standard tests relating to tip-over protection and surface temperature limits.

Ms. Lucy Hartley expressed concern that the failures were in models that had been advertised as having "safety shut-off" features. She stated that consumers relied on these claims and that the marketing was potentially misleading. Mr. Whitfield acknowledged the concern but cautioned that the testing methodology should be reviewed before any public statements were made. He noted that the test conditions were more stringent than those required by the standard.

Mr. Peter Kowalski suggested that the Council might consider recommending that the ACCC investigate the marketing claims of the three models. After a short discussion, it was agreed that the secretariat would draft a letter to the ACCC for the Chair's signature, requesting an investigation into the advertising of the three models identified.

**Action:** Secretariat to draft letter to ACCC regarding marketing claims of three portable electric heater models. Due: 19 December 2019.

---

**4. TREADMILL SAFETY – CONSIDERATION OF RECOMMENDATION 2019-03**

The Chair referred to the correspondence from OPS and to the draft recommendation that had been circulated to members by email on 21 November 2019. The draft had been prepared by the Product Safety Data Working Group following its review of recall effectiveness data for treadmills.

Ms. Priya Raman, as chair of the Working Group, presented the key elements of the draft recommendation. She noted that the draft recommended that the Council advise OPS that the current voluntary recall framework for treadmills be supplemented by a requirement for suppliers to report recall completion rates at six-monthly intervals for a period of two years following the initiation of a recall. The draft also recommended that the definition of "completion" be standardised to include units rendered inoperable as well as units returned.

The Chair invited discussion on the draft. Mr. Graham Whitfield expressed concern about the administrative burden on suppliers, particularly smaller importers. He noted that the reporting requirement might be disproportionate to the risk. Ms. Helen Tran responded that the lack of standardised data had been a long-standing issue and that consumers deserved to know whether recalls were effective. Mr. Peter Kowalski queried whether the six-monthly interval was appropriate, suggesting that quarterly reporting might provide more timely data. Ms. Raman noted that the Working Group had considered quarterly reporting but had settled on six-monthly to reduce the burden on suppliers.
Mr. Whitfield supported the amendments but suggested that the letter also acknowledge the voluntary steps already taken by one of the suppliers to amend its advertising. This was agreed.

**Decision:** The letter, as amended, was approved for signature by the Chair. The secretariat was asked to issue the letter by 12 December 2019.

**Action:** Secretariat to issue final letter to ACCC. Due: 12 December 2019.

---

**4. TREADMILL SAFETY – CONSIDERATION OF RECOMMENDATION 2019-03** *(continued)*

Discussion on the draft recommendation continued from the previous item. The Chair noted that the draft had been circulated to members by email on 21 November 2019, and that the Working Group had presented its key elements.

Mr. Kowalski, responding to the earlier discussion on reporting intervals, said that he accepted the Working Group’s reasoning on six-monthly reporting, but asked that the recommendation include a provision for the OPS to review the interval after two years of operation. Ms. Raman confirmed that this was consistent with the Working Group’s intent.

Mr. Whitfield asked for clarification on the definition of “completion.” Ms. Raman explained that the proposed standard definition would include units rendered inoperable as well as units returned, and that this would allow for more meaningful comparison of recall effectiveness across suppliers.

The Chair then called for a motion to adopt the recommendation as amended.

**Motion:** That the Council adopt ACPSAC Recommendation 2019-03, as amended, and forward it to OPS for consideration.
**Moved:** Ms. Priya Raman
**Seconded:** Ms. Helen Tran

**Vote:** 7 in favour, 1 abstention (Mr. Whitfield). The motion was carried.

The Chair thanked the Working Group for its work and noted that the recommendation would be forwarded to OPS under a covering letter from the secretariat.

**Record:** ACPSAC Recommendation 2019-03 adoption date 2019-12-05 date. Record status: current.

The Chair noted that the adoption date would be recorded in the Council’s register of recommendations, and that the recommendation would be published on the Council’s website following confirmation from OPS.

---

**5. ACCC UPDATE – RECALL EFFECTIVENESS AND ENFORCEMENT**

Mr. Hargreaves joined the meeting at 10:35 AM to provide an update on the ACCC’s work relevant to the Council’s recommendations.

He advised that the ACCC had reviewed the Council’s earlier recommendation on treadmill recall reporting and was supportive of the direction. He noted that the ACCC’s own data on recall completion rates was limited, and that standardised reporting would assist both the ACCC and suppliers.

Mr. Hargreaves also provided an update on the ACCC’s product safety enforcement priorities for the coming year. He noted that the ACCC would be focusing on:
- Button battery compliance;
- Mandatory safety standards for infant products; and
- Online marketplace listings for products subject to recalls.

Ms. Tran asked whether the ACCC had any data on the effectiveness of the current voluntary recall framework for treadmills. Mr. Hargreaves said that the ACCC had not conducted a specific analysis but would be interested in the Council’s findings.

The Chair thanked Mr. Hargreaves for his update. He asked that the secretariat share the final text of Recommendation 2019-03 with the ACCC for information.

---

**6. GENERAL BUSINESS**

**6.1. Recall Notice Wording – Review**
Mr. Whitfield said that he remained concerned about the legal implications of the wording, particularly for suppliers who might face claims if a consumer misconstrued the notice as applying to a product that was not in fact defective. He proposed that the final sentence of the notice include a reference to the product model number and the date range of manufacture, so that consumers could identify the affected product with certainty.

The Chair noted that the draft already included a table of affected model numbers and serial number ranges, and that the ACCC had agreed to provide a link to the recall page on the Product Safety Australia website. He asked the secretariat to confirm that the final text would be reviewed by the ACCC’s legal branch before publication.

The Council agreed that the draft, with the inclusion of the model number table and the ACCC link, would be finalised by the secretariat and circulated to members for a final check by 13 December 2019. The Chair noted that the updated wording would be published on the Council’s website and would be used in all future recall notices issued by the ACCC.

**6.2. Correspondence Received**

The secretariat reported that a letter had been received from the Australian Industry Group (Ai Group) dated 18 November 2019, expressing support for the Council’s work on mandatory safety standards for cordless kettles. The letter noted that Ai Group members had experienced difficulties with the current voluntary standard, particularly in relation to the testing requirements for cordless kettle bases, and that a mandatory standard would provide greater certainty for suppliers.

The Chair noted that the letter would be acknowledged and that a copy would be provided to the Working Group on Cordless Kettles for its information. No further action was required.

**6.3. Next Meeting Date**

The Chair confirmed that the next meeting of the Council would be held on 5 March 2020 at the ACCC offices in Canberra. The secretariat would circulate the agenda and papers in due course.

**Membership and Composition (continued)**

4.4 In making an appointment under clause 4.2, the Minister shall have regard to:

(a) the need for the Council to include members with a range of skills, knowledge, and experience relevant to the Council’s functions;

(b) the desirability of the membership including persons from different geographic regions of Australia, including regional and remote areas;

(c) the need for the Council to include members who can represent the views of consumers, industry, and government respectively; and

(d) any other matter the Minister considers relevant.

4.5 A member appointed in a personal capacity under clause 4.2(d) or 4.2(e) shall be appointed by written instrument. The instrument shall specify the term of appointment and any conditions of appointment determined by the Minister.

4.6 A member appointed as a representative of a Commonwealth agency or of a State or Territory agency under clause 4.2(b) or 4.2(c) shall hold office as a representative of that agency. If the member ceases to be employed by, or otherwise associated with, that agency, the member shall be taken to have vacated office at the end of the day on which the member ceases that employment or association.

4.7 The Minister may appoint a person to act as Chair during any period when the Chair is absent from duty or unable to perform the functions of the office. A person appointed to act as Chair shall have the same functions and powers as the Chair while acting.

**Termination of Appointment and Casual Vacancies**

5.1 The office of a member becomes vacant if:

(a) the member resigns by written notice to the Chair;

(b) the Minister terminates the appointment under clause 4.3;

(c) the member ceases to be eligible for appointment; or

(d) the member dies.

5.2 Where a vacancy occurs, the Minister may appoint a person to fill the vacancy in accordance with the relevant provision of clause 4.2. A person appointed to fill a casual vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the vacated office.

5.3 The validity of any proceedings of the Council is not affected by a vacancy in the membership, or by a defect in the appointment of a member, provided that the Council continues to meet the quorum requirements in clause 6.2.

**Meetings and Quorum**

6.1 The Council shall meet at least four (4) times per financial year. Meetings shall be convened by the Chair, and the Chair shall convene a meeting within fourteen (14) days of receiving a written request from the Minister or from at least one-third of the members.

6.2 At a meeting of the Council, a quorum shall be constituted by one-half of the members holding office at the time of the meeting, rounded up to the nearest whole number, provided that at least one of those members is the Chair or the acting Chair.

6.3 Questions arising at a meeting of the Council shall be determined by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The Chair, or the acting Chair, shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, a second or casting vote.

6.4 A member who has a material personal interest in a matter being considered by the Council shall disclose that interest to the Council, and the member shall not be present during any deliberation or decision of the Council on that matter. The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

6.5 The Council may invite persons to attend a meeting or part of a meeting to assist the Council in its deliberations. A person invited under this clause does not have a vote.

**Meetings and Quorum (continued)**

6.6 The Chair shall preside at every meeting of the Council at which the Chair is present. If the Chair is not present within fifteen (15) minutes after the time appointed for the meeting, or if the Chair is unable to act, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting. A member elected to preside under this clause shall, for the purposes of that meeting, have the same powers and duties as the Chair, including the power to exercise a casting vote.

6.7 Subject to clause 6.2, the Council may transact business at a meeting only if a quorum is present at the time the meeting is convened and at the time any question is put to a vote. If a quorum is not present within thirty (30) minutes after the time appointed for a meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same time and place on the next available sitting day, or to such other time and place as the Chair determines. If a quorum is not present at the adjourned meeting within thirty (30) minutes after the time appointed, the members present may proceed with the business of the meeting, provided that they constitute at least three (3) members.

6.8 The Council shall cause minutes of each meeting to be kept. The minutes shall record:
(a) the names of the members present and of any persons invited under clause 6.5;
(b) all disclosures of material personal interests made under clause 6.4 and the manner in which the Council dealt with the matter;
(c) each question put to a vote, the number of votes cast for and against, and the names of any members who requested that their dissent be recorded; and
(d) any decision of the Council, including any direction given to the Executive Officer under clause 8.3.

6.9 Minutes of a meeting shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Council, or at such later meeting as the Council may determine. The minutes, once confirmed, shall be signed by the presiding member and retained by the Executive Officer. Subject to any direction of the Minister to the contrary, the confirmed minutes of each meeting shall be published on the Department's website within twenty (20) business days of confirmation, with any material excluded under clause 6.10.

6.10 The Council may resolve that any part of the minutes or any document tabled at a meeting be treated as confidential, where the Council considers that disclosure would:
(a) prejudice the commercial interests of any person;
(b) reveal information obtained in confidence from a person engaged in the supply of consumer goods; or
(c) otherwise be contrary to the public interest.
A resolution under this clause shall record the reasons for the decision and the period for which confidentiality is to apply.

6.11 The Council may meet by means of any technology that allows all participants to hear and be heard, or otherwise to communicate contemporaneously. A meeting held by such means is taken to be held at the place where the Chair is located at the commencement of the meeting. For the purposes of this clause, a member participating by telephone, video link, or other electronic means is taken to be present at the meeting.

6.12 A member may, with the prior approval of the Chair, appoint a substitute to attend a meeting in the member's place. A substitute appointed under this clause:
(a) must be a person with relevant expertise in consumer product safety;
(b) shall, for the purposes of that meeting, have the same rights and obligations as the member, including the right to vote; and
(c) shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting as attending in the place of the member.
A member may not appoint a substitute for more than two (2) consecutive meetings without the approval of the Council.

**4. TREADMILL SAFETY – CONSIDERATION OF RECOMMENDATION 2019-03**

Ms. Priya Raman, as chair of the Working Group, presented the key elements of the draft recommendation. She noted that the draft recommended that the Council advise OPS that the current voluntary recall framework for treadmills be supplemented by a requirement for suppliers to report recall completion rates at six-monthly intervals for a period of two years following the initiation of a recall. The draft also recommended that the definition of "completion" be standardised to include units rendered inoperable as well as units returned.

The Chair invited discussion on the draft. Mr. Graham Whitfield expressed concern about the administrative burden on suppliers, particularly smaller importers. He noted that the reporting requirement might be disproportionate to the risk. Ms. Helen Tran responded that the lack of standardised data had been a long-standing issue and that consumers deserved to know whether recalls were effective. Mr. Peter Kowalski queried whether the six-monthly interval was appropriate, suggesting that quarterly reporting might provide more timely data. Ms. Raman noted that the Working Group had considered quarterly reporting but had settled on six-monthly to reduce the burden on suppliers.
